options: A versioned, installable dbt project — macros, and sometimes models and tests — written by dbt Labs or the community
A compressed backup of your own dbt project
A single CSV file loaded as a seed
A Stripe-style subscription tier for dbt Cloud
questions.explain: A package is someone else's dbt project (usually macros, sometimes models/tests too), versioned and installable into your own project.

questions.q: Where is a package declared, and what command installs it?
options: Declared in packages.yml, installed with dbt deps
Declared in dbt_project.yml, installed with dbt run
Declared in schema.yml, installed with dbt test
Packages install automatically with no declaration needed
questions.explain: packages.yml lists the packages and version ranges a project depends on; dbt deps downloads them into dbt_packages/.

questions.q: How do you call a macro from an installed package, like dbt_utils?
options: With the package name as a namespace prefix, e.g. dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key(...)
Package macros can't be called directly — only used internally by dbt
By copying the macro's code into your own macros/ folder first
By running a separate dbt package command before every use
questions.explain: Once installed, a package's macros are called the same way as your own macros, just prefixed with the package name as a namespace.

questions.q: Why does pinning a version range like `[">=1.1.0", "<2.0.0"]` matter?
options: It accepts patch and minor updates automatically while blocking a breaking major-version bump you haven't reviewed
It has no real effect — dbt always installs the latest version regardless
It forces the package to install in developer mode only
It disables all macros in the package except one
questions.explain: A version range lets safe updates flow in while protecting the project from an unreviewed breaking change in a new major version.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the main reason to use a package instead of writing the same logic yourself?
options: The problem (e.g. generating a consistent surrogate key) has often already been solved correctly by thousands of other projects
Packages run faster than any custom macro, in every case
Custom macros are not allowed alongside installed packages
Packages are required for every dbt project to compile at all
questions.explain: A well-maintained package has already handled the edge cases and been tested in production — reusing it avoids reinventing a solved problem, often with subtle bugs.
